insufficiency: Plans and summaries supported conclusions about artifacts that had not actually run.
Ambient and historical signals were promoted into mutation authority by underspecified briefs.
Local interventions duplicated or contradicted accepted plans before the failure class was identified.
Useful later work crossed unsatisfied dependency gates without an explicit program stop.
Carried state and unchanged retries produced plausible but non-comparable evidence.
Accumulated live controls allowed historical records to compete with the current authority surface.
Unvalidated proposals accumulated without increasing confidence or convergence.
C1, C2, and C5 did not prohibit secret-bearing evidence channels or require repair of an emitting path and contaminated context.

rule: Use direct authority and one human-readable canonical Program control.
insufficiency: Making those mechanisms optional did not stop agents from treating them as required live state.

rule: Continue a bounded objective across questions, status requests, and failed approaches.
insufficiency: Earlier continuity language was Program-focused and did not govern ordinary conversational steering.

rule: Require diagnostic evidence to select a decision and preserve unrelated failure planes.
insufficiency: A changed factor could satisfy the old rule even when its outcomes had no decision consumer.

rule: Predeclare operation claims and preserve each as SUPPORTED, REJECTED, or INCONCLUSIVE.
insufficiency: EvidenceReceipt v1 could preserve a terminal label without the claims needed for the next decision.

rule: Reset a contradicted working model before another mutation at that boundary.
insufficiency: Decision-focused instrumentation and one-factor retries did not require a model reset when authoritative facts disproved the interpretation driving those attempts.

rule: Preserve bounded observations while deciding only from claim-relevant facts, and end a diagnostic when those facts are complete and quiescent.
insufficiency: Claim-scoped receipts and decision-focused instrumentation did not prevent fixed reducers from hiding new structural states or unrelated context from rejecting a target claim.

rule: Classify diagnostic evidence by content and producer contract rather than treating a channel as automatically secret or safe.
insufficiency: The secret boundary prohibited secret-bearing logs but did not prevent blanket channel suppression from destroying safe decision-bearing diagnostics.

rule: End planning when the next useful action has a purpose, authority, and check; carry routine work through its usable outcome.
insufficiency: Smallest-action and just-in-time guidance left the end of planning implicit and allowed control activity or component evidence to substitute for completed outcomes.

rule: Record each human decision, dated and sourced, in the governing Program's Boundaries or in canonical project policy; remove its question in that revision, check those records before asking, keep the control in a tracker item, and make copies cite the control revision they project.
insufficiency: Needs from human held pending decisions and standing rules moved to project policy, but nothing said where a made decision goes, when its question leaves the control, or that copies cite their source, so settled decisions lived only in memories, comments, and state files and were asked again.

rule: Coordinate several Programs through a portfolio Program that settles priority, ownership, and conflicts between members without deciding their internal work or revising their controls; members report status and blockers to it.
insufficiency: One coordinator per control prevents two writers of a control but does not describe a coordinator whose subject is other Programs, leaving an orchestrator to edit controls it does not own or keep an uncited second source of priority.
